summary: Lake Superior light of 1858 at the mouth of the Eagle River, Keweenaw County; discontinued 1908, sold at auction; now a private vacation rental with grounds closed.

lens.where: sixth-order lens of the 1858 light; USLHS lists no current optic

structures.type: square tower built into the dwelling
structures.note: First tower. Height and material disputed: 19 ft stone (LighthouseFriends) vs 12 ft square brick, 24 ft tall (Pepper). Replaced by the second tower.

structures.type: square tower with conical lantern, integral to the keeper's dwelling
structures.note: 24 ft from base to lantern center (USLHS); standing

access.note: Privately owned since the 1908 auction; grounds, dwelling and tower closed; now a vacation rental (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Station lighted in 1858 (LighthouseFriends; USLHS established 1858). Pepper says construction was finished in 1857.
Large cracks found at the base of the tower
Congress set aside $14,000 for a replacement light; accounts differ on what followed (LighthouseFriends: reverted and re-provided 1871; Pepper: canceled July 1870)
Second (present) tower built into the dwelling, per USLHS
Walls rebuilt and the dwelling renovated
Board reports the light has outlived its usefulness and proposes moving it to Sand Hills
Act of 15 February 1893 authorizes the move at a cost not to exceed $20,000; no appropriation through the late 1890s
Board reports the river mouth blocked with sand and the dwelling in a far advanced state of decay
Discontinued in 1908 (LighthouseFriends, Pepper); the USLHS record says 1909
Sold at public auction on 2 August 1908 to John Vertin of Calumet for $925
Sand Hills light built, first keeper William R. Bennetts, brother of Thomas J. Bennetts (LighthouseFriends)
Private owner acquired the lighthouse (family purchase begun around 1996)
Most recent owner bought it; restored it; offered it as a vacation rental

notes_for_editor: Checked this round. 1892 report (scan p. 547) read in the corpus OCR: 'Sand Hills, 12 miles west of Eagle River' and, in the same passage, 'is 7 miles mmthwest of £agle Eiver' (southwest). Pepper says 'some seven miles to the west'. The story now gives both report figures and Pepper's. 1893 report (scan p. 210, entry 1235): 'The moving of this light to Sand Hills, at a cost not to exceed $20,000, was authorized by' the act of 15 Feb 1893. 1899 report (scan p. 222, entry 346): 'no appropriation therefor haa yet' has been made; now footnote 6, replacing the 1896-97 identifier that had no page. The 1900 report's Eagle River entry says the same statement was made in the Board's reports for 1894 through 1899, so 'late 1890s' is supported. 1901 report (entry 370): 'rock}^ reef about one-half mile offshore', 'An old dock ... is now rotten', 'blocked up with sand', 'far advanced state of decay'. The volume has no page index, so the printed page 126 is the OCR page head, not checked against an image; the scan page is not confirmed. The 1896 report (fiscal year ended June 30, 1896, entry 1431) also has the Eagle River statement; not cited now. LighthouseFriends read: 1845 Cliff Mine; 28 Sept 1850 $4,000; January 27, 1853 cession; July 17, 1854 contract; 1855 completion and the rejected work; lighted later in 1858; nineteen-foot stone tower and sixth-order lens; 1868 inspector's report quoted; 1869/1871 $14,000; second tower in NE corner of a brick dwelling; Griswold; Feiser (born Germany 1838, Cliff Mine engineer, 27th Michigan); Bennetts and the Manitou and Eagle Harbor stints; 1892 'outlived its usefulness'; 1908 discontinuance; 2 Aug 1908 auction to John Vertin of Calumet for $925; 1919 Sand Hills; ownership history (owner names omitted, living-people rule); vacation rental; grounds closed. Pepper read: $6,500 on 28 Sept 1850; completion 1857; first tower 12-ft square brick, 24 ft, one-and-a-half-story yellow brick dwelling, ten nautical miles; 1867 cracks; $14,000 recalled 12 July 1870; Cliff Mine closed 1873 and the mouth silted; 1884 walls rebuilt; 1908 auction (Major Charles Keeler, Eleventh District); four-unit condominium. USLHS place record read: established 1858; tower 1874 stone; quarters stone; discontinued 1909; 'Open to Public: No'; principal and first-assistant lists match the JSON roster (four principal keepers, Julia listed as principal). CONFLICTS LEFT OPEN: (1) first tower: LighthouseFriends 19-ft stone tower vs Pepper 12-ft square brick, 24 ft; (2) second tower's dwelling: LighthouseFriends brick vs USLHS stone; (3) completion and lighting: LighthouseFriends completed 1855, lighted 1858; Pepper completed 1857; USLHS established 1858; (4) 1850 appropriation: $4,000 (LighthouseFriends) vs $6,500 (Pepper); (5) 1869 money: LighthouseFriends reverted and re-provided 1871 vs Pepper recalled July 1870; (6) discontinuance 1908 (LighthouseFriends, Pepper) vs 1909 (USLHS); (7) Sand Hills distance: 12 miles west and 7 miles southwest in the same 1892 passage, and 7 miles west in Pepper. The 1868 Board report is known only through LighthouseFriends' quotation (no 1868 volume in the corpus). The NRHP nomination (80004839) was not readable: the cached PDF is an image, so the NRHP listing year (1984 in the record) is unverified and not used. Thomas Bennetts' Manitou (about 1908 to 1913) and Eagle Harbor (about 1913 to 1927) stints are approximate, from LighthouseFriends' 'five years' and 'fourteen years'. Newspapers were not searched for this station.
